messages:
maya_support: FYI customer on Dedicated (vpc-az-3) started getting 401s for SSO-only endpoints ~10:05 UTC after IdP key rotation. Error in our auth proxy logs: 'kid not found'. They say traffic goes through our dedicated edge proxy -> internal ext_authz. Can infra take a look?

kevin_eng-infra: Thanks, Maya. Do we have a repro HTTP capture or example JWT that failed? Also which proxy (dedicated-auth-proxy v2.3.1?) and LB type (NLB vs ALB)?

maya_support: Customer says NLB + internal dedicated-auth-proxy (daemonset). They supplied one failing Authorization header payload (redacted):

customer-jane: FYI this is our request (sensitive parts replaced):

curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6IjE2MG...' https://api.customer.svc/private

maya_support: From our proxy logs (trimmed):

```
2026-03-17T09:05:12Z auth-proxy[1234]: validate_jwt: kid=160a... not found in cached keyset (issuer=https://idp.example/.well-known/jwks.json)
2026-03-17T09:05:12Z auth-proxy[1234]: ext_authz_response: 401 Unauthorized -> inbound service
```

maya_support: Customer confirmed they rotated keys at 09:02 UTC (IdP logs). IdP now serves new JWKS with new kid. They see successful validation if they hit IdP directly. Suggests our proxy is using stale JWKS.

carlos_sre: Can you paste the proxy's jwks fetch logs? We have a known edge case where the JWKS cache TTL was ignored in 2.3.1 if the IdP returns Cache-Control: no-cache; we previously saw caching for 5m. If that matches, a restart or cache flush fixes it.

maya_support: I captured a snippet from the proxy stdout around 09:00-09:07: 

```
[08:58:50] jwks_fetch: fetched https://idp.example/.well-known/jwks.json status=200 cache-control="no-cache, no-store"
[09:00:02] jwks_cache: using cached jwks (age=182s)
[09:05:12] validate_jwt: kid=160a... lookup failed
```

kevin_eng-infra: That lines up. Looks like the proxy ignored Cache-Control and used a cached copy. Two quick mitigation options: 1) flush JWKS cache on the dedicated-auth-proxy (admin endpoint) or 2) restart the daemonset pod (fast). Which can you run?

maya_support: Customer prefers we avoid restarts during business hours. Is there an admin endpoint to clear keys?

kevin_eng-infra: Yes — the auth-proxy exposes /admin/keys/flush (POST). Example (from control plane):

```
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>' \
  https://dedicated-auth-proxy.internal/admin/keys/flush
```

kevin_eng-infra: After that the proxy will re-fetch the JWKS on next validation. You can also force a re-fetch by hitting /health?probe=force (but admin flush is preferred).

maya_support: Sent the flush command on the customer's behalf and watching logs.

maya_support: Log after flush: 

```
09:07:03 jwks_fetch: cache flushed by admin API
09:07:04 jwks_fetch: fetched https://idp.example/.well-known/jwks.json status=200 cache-control="no-cache, no-store"
09:07:04 validate_jwt: kid=160a... found -> allow
```

customer-jane: Confirmed from their side: requests succeeded after your flush. Thanks. :tada:

carlos_sre: Root cause notes for postmortem: dedicated-auth-proxy v2.3.1 had a bug where it treated missing/max-age heuristics incorrectly and persisted JWKS for a default TTL (300s) even when the IdP specified no-cache. This interacts poorly with rapid key rotation.

kevin_eng-infra: Action items:
- Patch scheduled: update proxy to 2.3.2 that respects Cache-Control and supports forced revalidation on 304 responses.
- Add an admin metric jwks_cache_age & alert if age > 60s for high-security tenants.
- Add runbook step: use /admin/keys/flush prior to pod restarts for JWKS rotation incidents.

maya_support: I'll follow up with customer summary and link to runbook steps.

customer-jane: Appreciate the quick turnaround. One ask: can you notify customers when we detect backend JWKS rotations causing errors? It would save our on-call time.

kevin_eng-infra: Good suggestion. We'll add a detection alert that correlates kid-not-found spikes with jwks_fetch success/failure and surface a customer-facing incident note if we see >5% 401 spike for 3 minutes.

maya_support: Marking this resolved for the customer. Filing internal ticket INFRA-4321 to track the patch and alert work.

carlos_sre: Leaving a debug tip here: if you need to validate JWKS quickly from a machine, run: 

```
python -c "import jwcrypto.jwk as j; import requests; print(requests.get('https://idp.example/.well-known/jwks.json').text)"
```

kevin_eng-infra: Also FYI — avoid deploying 2.3.1 to new high-rotation tenants. Patch ETA 2026-03-20.

maya_support: Thanks everyone. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
